answers.answer: Leave 4 tokens of each gem color and all 5 gold tokens. Reveal 3 nobles. Remove the other nobles from the game permanently.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments: 2 players: 4 per color, 5 gold, 3 nobles. Setup: 'Remove remaining noble tiles from the game'.

answers.answer: For 3 players use 5 gem tokens per color, 5 gold and 4 nobles. For 4 players use 7 gem tokens per color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more gems per color and one more noble, with no change in gold.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count: 3 | 5 | 5 | 4; 4 | 7 | 5 | 5.

answers.answer: Shuffle the three development decks separately. Arrange them in a column with level 1 at the bottom, level 2 in the middle and level 3 at the top. Reveal 4 cards from each deck, making 12 face-up cards in a 3x4 grid. The youngest player starts and play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player: 'The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise.'

answers.answer: Choose exactly one action: take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different colors; take 2 non-gold gems of one color only if at least 4 of that color are in supply before taking; reserve 1 development if you have fewer than 3 reserved cards and take 1 gold if available; or buy 1 face-up development or 1 development reserved on a previous turn by paying its cost after bonuses, using gold as substitutes if desired. You cannot take gems and buy in the same turn, or reserve and then buy that card in the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'must perform exactly one' of the four actions; purchase includes '1 card you reserved on a previous turn'.

answers.answer: All tokens you own must remain visible to all players at all times, including gold.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times.'

answers.answer: You may take 2 green from the pile of 4, leaving 2. You cannot take 2 red from the pile of 3. Check the minimum of 4 before taking the tokens. Neither gem-taking action permits gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them'; both gem actions specify no gold.

answers.answer: Temporarily holding 12 is allowed. Return 2 tokens of your choice to finish with 10. These may include gems just drawn. Gold counts toward the 10-token limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: may 'temporarily exceed 10'; return tokens 'of their choice'; 'some or all of the tokens they just took'; '(including gold)'.

answers.answer: Reserve 1 card and take 1 gold, temporarily increasing your tokens from 10 to 11. Return 1 token of your choice, possibly that gold, to end at 10. If gold is empty, you may still reserve and take no gold, staying at 10 tokens.
answers.evidence: Reserve: 'If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold.' Token Hand Limit permits returning gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: You may reserve 1 face-up market development or the top card from any one of the three level decks. Take a deck card without showing it to opponents. Only the player who reserved a card may later buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'face-up' or 'top card'; 'without revealing it'; 'only ... the player who reserved them'.

answers.answer: You cannot reserve while holding 3 reserved cards, including merely to obtain gold. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; buying it is the only way it leaves your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: 'If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another'; 'The only way to remove a reserved card ... is to purchase it.'

answers.answer: Immediately fill the reserved face-up level-2 card's space with the top card of the level-2 deck. Purchasing a face-up card likewise immediately refills its space from its own level deck. Buying a reserved card removes nothing from the market, so causes no market refill. If the relevant deck is empty, the acquired face-up card's space stays empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: 'Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced'; empty deck: 'empty space ... remains empty'.

answers.answer: The 2 blue bonuses cover both blue costs, so spend 1 green token, or 1 gold substituting for green. If bonuses cover every required color, spend no tokens. Bonuses remain permanently and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules give this exact blue/green example; bonuses are 'permanent'; gold substitutes 'for any single gem token'; enough bonuses permit buying 'without spending any tokens'.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses leave a cost of 1 blue, 1 black and 1 white. Spend your blue token for blue and one gold each for black and white. All three spent tokens return to supply. Your purchased bonus cards stay with you and retain their permanent bonuses.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce tokens needed; gold substitutes for any single gem; spent gem and gold tokens return to supply. Bonus Stacking calls bonuses permanent.

answers.answer: Buy 1 face-up development from the grid or 1 card reserved on a previous turn, paying its cost after applicable bonuses and any gold substitutions. Place purchased cards face up before you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so their bonuses and prestige values remain visible to everyone at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card and Turn Structure; 'face-up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible'.

answers.answer: No: 2 white bonuses plus a white or gold token do not meet the required 3 white bonuses. Acquiring a third white bonus makes you qualify at the end of that turn, with the 3 blue and 3 green bonuses. Bonuses above any requirement are allowed.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: qualify with 'at least' the shown bonuses; 'bonuses only ... not gem tokens'.

answers.answer: Choose exactly 1 of the two nobles; you cannot take both or decline all visits. The visit uses no action, gives 3 prestige, and eligibility is checked at the end of your turn after your action and token-limit check.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: automatic, cannot refuse, 'choose one', 'at most one noble per turn', 'not an action', 3 points. Turn Structure gives the check order.

answers.answer: Place the acquired noble tile face up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: 'Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.'

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns. A does not take another turn, since A already acted in this round. B is not guaranteed to win: compare everyone's prestige after D's turn, and another player may surpass B.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete the current round so everyone has the same number of turns. End-of-Game Clarifications: triggering player may be surpassed in the final round.

answers.answer: Your total becomes 16. This triggers the end condition because it is 15 or more, even though you skipped exactly 15. Finish the current round to equalize turns, then determine the winner by most prestige with the stated tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Nobles are 3 points; End-Game Trigger: '15 or more'; winner is most points 'at the end of the final round'.

answers.answer: B wins. A and B tie at 16 prestige, above C's 15, and B has fewer purchased developments, 9 versus A's 10. Nobles count toward prestige. B's 3 unpurchased reserved cards do not count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner: most prestige, noble points included. Tiebreaker: 'fewest development cards' purchased. Purchase rules distinguish reserved cards from purchased cards.

answers.answer: No. The 8 printed points on unpurchased reserved cards do not count for scoring or the 15-point trigger, and their 2 white bonuses do not reduce costs or qualify for nobles. Those benefits belong to purchased developments.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: 'Printed on each purchased card'; Payment rules: 'previously purchased development cards'; Noble Visits: bonuses 'from purchased development cards'.

answers.answer: You receive no physical blue token. The purchased card provides a permanent blue discount for future purchases and its blue bonus can help meet a noble requirement despite its zero prestige value.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: 'never generate tokens'; each purchased card adds one permanent bonus. Components permit a prestige value of 0; nobles require card bonuses.

answers.answer: No: its own blue bonus cannot pay for buying it, since only previously purchased cards reduce that purchase's cost; you lack the needed blue token or gold. A white bonus acquired by a legal purchase does count for the noble check at the end of that same turn.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses from 'previously purchased' cards. Noble Visits checks bonuses from purchased cards 'at the end of their turn'.

answers.answer: The blue bonuses cover the 1 blue cost. The 3 excess blue bonuses cannot cover green or produce change in blue tokens. You still owe 2 green, payable with 2 green tokens, 2 gold, or 1 green and 1 gold.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess in a color gives 'no benefit for that purchase (no
is given)'; bonuses reduce their color; gold substitutes for any single gem.

answers.answer: The bonuses were not used up; they are permanent. If the other noble remains available and your cards stay unchanged, taking 1 gem from each of 3 different available non-gold colors, or legally taking 2 of one non-gold color with at least 4 in supply beforehand, can still be followed by receiving that noble at the end of your next turn. You cannot collect it during an opponent's intervening turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses are permanent; multiple nobles: 'other noble(s) remain available for future turns'; nobles are checked at the end of the player's turn, at most one per turn.

answers.answer: Yes. With no reserved cards you may reserve that 1 face-up level-3 card regardless of its purchase cost. Reserving does not require paying its printed cost, and you take 1 gold if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve action: take one face-up card or top card of any deck, maximum 3 reserved, and take 1 gold if available. Payment is specified under purchasing, not reserving.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled by taking the top level-2 deck card into your reserved hand. All 12 face-up market cards remain. You reserve only 1 card, so cannot take a second replacement card into your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserve: 'Take one development card'; top-deck reservation is separate from a face-up reservation. Card replacement applies to face-up cards acquired from the grid.

answers.answer: The 4 face-up cards remain available: you may buy 1 if you can pay, or reserve 1 if you have fewer than 3 reserved cards, taking 1 gold if available. Purchasing one leaves its space empty permanently; the other 3 stay available.
answers.evidence: Purchase allows a face-up card; reserve allows a face-up card. Card Replacement: if corresponding deck is empty, 'empty space ... remains empty for the rest of the game'.

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy 1 affordable card reserved on a previous turn, or take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different available colors. These are separate action choices; choose exactly one.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: exhaustion 'does not end the game'; continue remaining legal actions 'including purchasing reserved cards'. Turn Structure lists the three-color action.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different available colors, temporarily hold 13, and return all 3 newly taken tokens to finish at 10 with unchanged holdings. No net token gain is required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: may temporarily exceed 10 and 'may return some or all of the tokens they just took'.

answers.answer: A returns both spent gold to supply, rather than removing them from the game. B reserves 1 card and takes 1 of those gold, since B holds fewer than 3 reserved cards. Exactly 1 gold remains in supply immediately after B takes gold, before any token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply.' Reserving takes 1 gold if available.

answers.answer: Yes, you may buy the 1 face-up level-3 card now by paying its cost after any bonuses and gold substitutions. The purchase action allows face-up cards without any lower-level ownership prerequisite.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: 'Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost shown on the card.'

answers.answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble visit. The development raises you from 12 to 15, and the noble adds 3 for a total of 18 after your turn. Other players who have yet to act in the current round continue taking their turns to equalize turn counts.
answers.evidence: Noble visit 'automatic' and cannot be refused; noble worth 3. End trigger completes the current round for the same number of turns.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes the turn, including any end-of-turn checks. A does not start another round and nobody receives an extra turn, because A, B, C and D already have equal turn counts when D finishes that round.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns'.

answers.answer: Do not reveal a replacement noble from the seven removed tiles: they are out of the game permanently. Place the acquired tile face up in front of its recipient. Of the original 3 revealed nobles, 2 remain available in the middle.
answers.evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: 'Noble tiles removed during setup are out of the game permanently.' Received noble goes face up in front of the player.

answers.answer: Emerald is green; diamond is white; sapphire is blue; onyx is black; ruby is red; gold joker is yellow. There are 90 development cards: 40 level 1, 30 level 2 and 20 level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token-color table and Development Cards table (90 total; levels 1/2/3: 40/30/20).

answers.answer: You may pay 1 gold as a substitute for the 1 green cost and keep your green token; the summary does not require using the matching gem first. The spent gold returns to supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Gold tokens (jokers) can substitute for any single gem token. Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply.'

answers.answer: Yes. Take 1 red, 1 blue and 1 green. The four-token minimum applies only to taking 2 gems of the same color. The piles then contain 0 red, 1 blue and 2 green.
answers.evidence: Different-colors action: 'Take 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles.' Same-color action alone requires at least 4.

answers.answer: A direct exchange of 1 gold for 1 red is not among the four required action choices and is not a permitted use described by the joker purchase rule. Gold can substitute for any single gem token when paying to purchase a development, then returns to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists exactly four actions; Gold Token Specifics: gold substitutes for any gem color 'when purchasing a card'.

answers.answer: You cannot voluntarily pass when legal actions are available. You must choose exactly one: take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different colors; take 2 non-gold gems of one color with at least 4 in supply before taking; reserve 1 card if holding fewer than 3 reserved cards and take 1 gold if available; or buy 1 face-up or previously reserved development by paying its cost after bonuses and any gold substitutions.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: a player 'must perform exactly one of the following four actions'.

answers.answer: Sort gem and gold tokens by color into 6 distinct piles and place them within reach of all players.
answers.evidence: Setup step 5: '6 distinct piles sorted by color, within reach of all players'.

answers.answer: Your final prestige score is 15: 12 from purchased developments plus 3 from the noble. The 4 unspent gold and 5 other gem tokens add no prestige points.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources lists purchased development values and nobles at 3 each; no token scoring source is listed.

answers.answer: Shuffle the noble tiles before revealing the player-count-plus-one selection. Hand-picking preferred nobles does not follow this shuffled setup procedure.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4: 'Shuffle the noble tiles. Reveal a number of noble tiles equal to the number of players plus one'.
